disease_name: Gastrointestinal infections, Traveler's diarrhea, Intestinal overgrowth syndrome, Hepatic encephalopathy, Diverticulitis, Inflammatory bowel disease
indication: Acute gastrointestinal infections, Diarrhea of travelers, Intestinal overgrowth syndrome, Hepatic encephalopathy, Uncomplicated diverticulitis, Chronic inflammation of intestines, Prevention of infectious complications at colorectal surgical interventions, Gastrointestinal infections caused by bacteria sensitive to rifaximin
single_dose: Adults and children more senior than 12 years: from 200 mg each 8 hours – up to 400 mg each 8-12 hours (corresponding to 600-1200 mg of rifaximin a day). Children of 6-12 years: from 200 mg each 8-12 hours up to 400 mg each 12 hours (corresponding to 400-800 mg of rifaximin a day). Prevention of infectious complications in the pre- and post-operative period: Adults and children more senior than 12 years: on 400 mg each 12 hours. Children of 6-12 years: on 200-400 mg each 12 hours. In complex treatment of hyperammonemia: Adults and children more senior than 12 years: on 400 mg each 8 hours. Children of 6-12 years: on 200-300 mg each 8 hours.
dosage_frequency: Once daily, twice a day, every 8 hours
side_effects: Dizziness, Headache, Nausea, Vomiting, Abdominal pain, Diarrhea, Flatulence, Loss of appetite, Urticarial skin rash, Allergic reactions
unsuitable_population: Increased individual sensitivity to any of the drug components and also to other antibiotics of the Rifamycin group, Intestinal obstruction, Ulcerative colitis
